answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the ridge hash is checked against the jetty checkpoint at intake, the harbor audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 110 identities multiplies that fee by 260 with no matching gain in influence. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
